Use for: romance and love stories that have a more positive, lighter and more comforting, feel-good or uplifting approach to telling the story, and that tend not to create any anxiety, often featuring narratives around hope and optimism, friends or friendship, found or chosen family, communities, and where conflicts or crisis are usually resolved through communication and understanding, with the help of community and friends

Use for: Romance stories featuring or set in a working environment, or about a relationship with a work colleague or a romance with a person who is doing some work or working for the other person, for example, someone who is helping to renovate a building, doing some long-term construction work, the gardener, the boss, the CEO, the bodyguard, etc

Also class here: sweetheart romance. Use for: romance that does not contain any strong language or physical intimacy. Use with: FW for religious romance, faith-driven romance, or inspirational romance, and with 5PG* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate to indicate a wholesome romance with themes inspired by a particular spiritual belief or faith or with other FR* codes for wholesome romances that are also considered part of another genre romance, with 5PB-US-B for Amish romance, 5PGM for Christian romance, 5PGP for Muslim romance, etc

Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers to describe setting and TIME PERIOD 3* for historical settings

Also class here: Romance stories featuring extramarital love affairs, cheating love triangles, love triangle jealousy, or other stories featuring some sort of love triangle. Use for: romance stories where the main characters initially have a relationship based on friendship that gradually changes into a strong attraction
Also class here: Rivals to lovers’ romance, Frenemies. Use for: romance stories where the main characters initially have a conflicting relationship that gradually changes into a strong attraction

Also class here: fake-dating, false relationships, fake boyfriend or girlfriend, marriage of convenience romances. Use for: romance stories where the main characters initially have some sort of fake or pretend romantic relationship

Also class here: Stuck together romances, Only-one-bed romances, road trip romances, trapped together romances. Use for: romance stories where the main characters initially are thrown together into close proximity for various reason
Use for: a romance story that also involves a mystery, crime, suspense or thriller storyline but remains primarily a romance story. Use with: other F* genre fiction codes as appropriate

Also class here: Athlete Romance, Football romance, hockey romance, baseball romance, cricket romance, soccer romance, etc. Use for: Romance featuring participants in sports, sports stars, athletes, coaches, owners, agents, sports teams, sporting events, sporting activities or any romance where the sports element is an integral part of the story. Use with: S* codes to indicate which sport is the key aspect of the romance story

Also class here: military, armed services, armed forces, security, sailors, aircrew, law enforcement, soldiers, sheriffs, cops, firefighters, police, pilots, cabin crew etc. Use for: romance stories where one or more of the main protagonists is in a job that means wearing a formal uniform
Use for: romance stories featuring doctors, nurses, surgeons, veterinarians, or any professional medical setting, such as a hospital or clinic, etc

Also class here: Rockstar romance, Rags to riches romance, Millionaire or Billionaire romance, Secret Billionaire romance, Celebrity romance, Royal romance. Also class here: ‘why choose’ romances, harem or reverse harem romances, polyamory romance. Also class here: vampire romance, were / shifter romance, supernatural romance, monster romance, alien romance, fantasy romance, paranormal romance. Use for: genre romance stories where the themes are darker, usually featuring an anti-hero or non-heroic characters and/or distressing situations, often exploring themes such as the darker side of power dynamics in a relationship, questionable morals or ethics, they may feature trauma and violence, or they may deal with darker psychological themes of evil or horror in society. Also class here: Rebel and outsider romance, Mafia romance, Mob romance, MC Romance, Motorcycle Club Romance, Rogues, Rebels, and Rakes romance, Bad boy romance, Bad girl romance, Alpha Male romance, Bully romance, Biker romance, MMA romance, Fighter romance, or romances featuring characters such as assassins, criminals, outlaws, bandits, or morally grey characters. Use for: romance genre stories where one of the main protagonist is often a very strong, possessive, confident, and dominant male or female character, or romances where the main character works for, or is involved with, crime or criminal organisations, or is seen as an anti-hero, a wrongdoer, an outsider, or to have a bad or dangerous character, or is morally ambiguous, but the “bad” character will usually have a redeeming side or a change during the story. Use with: FJ* for action and adventure stories, with FHR or FFL for romance stories featuring organised crime, and with INTEREST 5* Qualifiers as appropriate. Prefer: FRV for romance stories with darker themes Taip pat žr.: FRV
Meilės romanai su detaliomis sekso scenomis; atitinkamai pridėtina ir 5X žymą Taip pat žr.: FP

Code.CodeDescription: Amerikietiškosios ir britiškosios tradicijos komiksai ir grafiniai romanai
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: comic-strip narratives that are part of or have been inspired by the styles associated with the comic book traditions that originated in the United States. These often feature super-hero style characters or heightened realities and were originally published in the traditional 32 page comic. They are usually part of a larger, serialised narrative, universe or story-arc that may have been published over a long period of time. This style has inspired many comics around the world and use of this code does not mean the comic is published or created in the USA, only that the work is seen as being an example of that style of comic book

Code.CodeDescription: Literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams, mokomoji literatūra
Code.CodeNotes: Use all Y* codes for: material aimed at, or purposefully written or created for a juvenile or adolescent audience (except for graphic novels, comic books, manga in X*). DO NOT USE: code ‘Y’ itself, but select specific categories from section Y*. Use all Y* codes with: only one INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifier to indicate a guideline starting interest age (detailed age ranges should be included in other metadata) – or for YP* use EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* qualifiers. All other qualifiers can be used as appropriate with Y* codes. DO NOT USE for: material intended primarily for adults that may also appeal to older teenagers. For ‘new adult’ content see note at 5LKE, for ‘Young Adult’ use the most appropriate 5A* Qualifier according to local usage of the term. NB: Y* codes should be used along with X* codes for graphic novels, comic books, manga. Y* codes may be used in combination with A*– W* codes but always prefer Y* codes and if mixing Y* codes with A*– W* codes, the Y* code must ALWAYS be designated as the Main Subject and sent with one 5A* qualifier. If sending A*– W* codes as Main Subject, then Y* codes should NOT be included except for JNU / JNUM with YP* or DSYC for reviews or critiques

Paveikslėlių knygelės, turinčios aiškią pasakojimo liniją Taip pat žr.: XA* XQ*

Also class here: books to colour in, magic painting books, books and painting sets, fingerprinting, rubber stamps, connect the dots, dot to dot, paint-by-numbers, stencil books, doodles, finger painting, learning to draw or paint, books to draw in, etc Taip pat žr.: YNA

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikiškos veiklos knygelės su užslėptu objektu
Code.CodeNotes: Autostereogramų knygelės ar knygelės, kuriose vaikas turi paveikslėliuose įžvelgti kokį nors daiktą ar veikėją Taip pat žr.: YNVP

Also class here: origami, books of paper dolls to dress, paper models to make or assemble, things to cut out or punch-out, dioramas, paper folding, or other activities for children using paper or card
YBL* kodai naudotini tik ikimokyklinio amžiaus vaikams skirtai medžiagai
Abėcėlės ar pirmiausiai ištariamų žodžių knygelės

Code.CodeDescription: Ankstyvoji vaikystė: eilės, rimai ir žodžių žaismas
Code.CodeNotes: Folkloro smulkieji žanrai ir nesudėtingi posmai labai mažiems vaikams (greitakalbės ir panašiai) Taip pat žr.: YDP YFV

Also class here: Pre-handwriting skills, pregraphism or pre-graphics skills and activities, writing readiness skills, activities for learning to hold a pen or pen or pencil control and skills, tracing exercises and activities, tracing different types of lines, patterns and shapes. Use for: works that help children acquire the fundamental skills children need to develop before they are able to write or draw

Code.CodeDescription: Ankstyvoji vaikystė: laikas ir metų laikai
Code.CodeNotes: Literatūra, skirta išmokyti pažinti valandas, skirti paros metą, savaitės dienas, metų laikus ir panašiai
Also class here: baby animals
Lietaratūra apie rutininius dalykus labai mažiems vaikams: kaip ir kodėl praustis, kada eiti miegoti, kaip sėstis ant naktipuodžio ir panašiai

Code.CodeDescription: Early years: potty and toilet training
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: titles that talk about poo, wee and farts. Use for: works that explain bodily functions linked to going to the toilet, as well as titles for teaching children how to use a potty or toilet
Also class here: sounds and noises, touch and feel, tastes and smells, fingers and toes, smiles and laughter, faces, peek-a-boo, hide-and-seek, etc
Use with: YXF* codes as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Ankstyvoji vaikystė: kaip ir kas veikia
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: books on ships, planes, trains, trucks, cars, bikes, buses, diggers, tractors, and other moving vehicles for the very young

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra, antologijos, almanachai
Code.CodeNotes: Pateikę reikiamą YD* kodą, kai įmanoma, taip pat nurodykite ir atitinkamą amžiaus ar žinių lygį žymintį kodą 5A*

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: kasmetiniai leidiniai
Code.CodeNotes: Kasmetinių leidinių atveju pirmiausia pateiktinas YDA kodas, o tada jau, jei įmanoma, nurodytini ir atitinkamą žanrą ar sritį žymintys kodai

Kai įmanoma, naudotinas kartu su kitu kodu, žyminčiu atitinkamą literatūros žanrą, pavyzdžiui – YF*, jei tai prozos antologija, ar YDP, jei tai poezijos antologija. Jei antologija apima įvairias literatūros formas, naudoti tik šį vieną kodą
Taip pat žr.: YBLB YFV

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: proza ir tikros istorijos
Code.CodeNotes: Pateikę reikiamą YF* kodą VISADA nurodykite ir atitinkamą amžiaus grupę ar žinių lygį žumintį 5A* kodą. Jei knygoje yra iššaukiančių scenų, pateikite ir 5X kogą. Be to, jei tai kūrinyne aiškiai išreikšta ir svarbu, galima pateikti ir atitinkamos GEOGRAFINĖS VIETOS ar LAIKOTARPIO žymes. Tais atvejais, kai vien tik YF* kodas nėra pakankamas, prieš jį pateikite ir atitinkamą specifinę temą žymintį YN* kodą. YDC kodas nurodytinas, jei tai rozos antologija. Jei kūrinyje aptariamos specifinės socialinės ar asmeninės problemos, prieš YF kodą pateikite ir atitinkamą YX* kodą. Jei tai komiksas, naudokite reikiamą X* kodą Taip pat žr.: XA* XQ*

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: klasikinė proza
Code.CodeNotes: Vaikams ir paaugliams skirti romanai ar trumpoji proza, išleisti iki 1960 m., arba vėlesni, bet visuotinai žanro klasika pripažįstami kūriniai

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: bendroji literatūra
Code.CodeNotes: Skirta visai šiuolaikinei vaikų ir paauglių nežanrinei literatūrai

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: veiksmo ir nuotykių literatūra
Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: interaktyvios nuotykių istorijos
Code.CodeNotes: Tradicinės ar skaitmeninės knygos, kuriose skaitytojui leidžiama pasirinkti iš galimų variantų, kaip pasakojimas plėtosis toliau. Kai įmanoma, po šio kodo pateikite ir atitinkamą YF* kodą, nusakantį kūrinio žanrą Taip pat žr.: YFZW

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: detektyvai ir paslapties romanai
Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: karo romanai
Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: siaubo, vaiduoklių romanai
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: scary stories of the paranormal, gothic ghost stories, contemporary and realistic horror stories. Use for: any story that is written to be scary or to give an age appropriate feeling of fear, including stories that turn out not to be scary, stories that feature ghosts (friendly or scary), monsters (frightening or misunderstood), witches (wicked or misrepresented), creepy settings, characters or beings, haunted houses or is any form of supernatural chilling, spooky or scary story. Use with: YNX* codes for stories about specific supernatural or paranormal beings, such as YNXB3 for ghost stories, or other YF* codes, such as YFQ for funny or comedy ghost or horror stories, YFJM for cautionary tales, YFH* for fantasy scary stories, YFHG for horror stories based on myths, YFHT for Dark fantasy horror stories, YFA for classic ghost or horror stories, etc Taip pat žr.: YNXW

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: distopiniai ir utopiniai pasakojimai, spekuliatyvioji literatūra
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: fiction set in dystopian or utopian societies, alternative history fiction. Use with: YFG or other YF* codes if possible

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic stories
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: end of the world stories, dying earth, collapsing or collapsed civilizations. Use for: stories set in worlds trying to prevent, or experiencing or that have already been affected by an apocalypse event, such as runaway climate change, an impact event, resource depletion, nuclear holocaust, pandemics, end times, zombie apocalypse, cybernetic revolts, technological singularity, invasion from space, dysgenics, etc
Use for: stories for children or teenagers with a superhero character or where the main characters are depicted as superheroes

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: mokslinė fantastika
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: YNTT for Time travel, time slip, or time loop sci-fi stories, YNXF for stories about extra-terrestrials or UFOs, YNNZ for stories about space travel, YNTC for stories about AI, Mecha, robots or new technology, etc

Also class here: Galactic empires, interstellar or intergalactic wars. Use for: science fiction stories set in space, in imagined galaxies or universes, or on different planets, often with advanced cultures and sophisticated technology and usually featuring main characters who are children or teenagers

Also class here: dieselpunk, cyberpunk, retrofuturism. Use for: science fiction based on an alternative world where, for example in the case of steampunk, 19th century steam power has emerged as the dominant technology

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: maginė fantastika (fentezi) ir magiškasis realizmas
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: paranormal fantasy, enchanted journeys, alternative worlds, accidental travel, portal fantasy, Isekai. Use all YFH* codes with: YNX* codes as appropriate, with YNXB* codes for stories featuring the paranormal or particular supernatural beings

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Epic fantasy / heroic fantasy
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: sword and sorcery fantasy, quest fantasy, high fantasy

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Magical realism / Magical fantasy
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Magical girl. Use for: works that incorporates fantastic, magical, mythical or supernatural elements into an otherwise real-world or mundane setting, or works where the magic itself – whether a magical object or a character with magical powers – is the subject of the story, rather than simply a means to an end. Use with: YNXW for stories about witches, wizards or magicians or YNXB* codes for other magical creatures

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Mythic fantasy / Myths and Legends fiction
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Myths or legends from any culture told or retold as fiction or in story form, mythological fiction, Arthurian fantasy, Classical fantasy (based on Greek and Roman myths), Shenmo (Gods and Demons), etc. Use for: fiction that is inspired by, or a retelling of, or that in some way draws from the characters, stories or themes of myth, legend, for example, a story based on a popular myth or character from a classic work in a modern setting or a story based on a minor character’s perspective, or that takes a ‘what if’ approach or create a mashup of different genres, for example, legendary character or hero meets dystopian future, or mythology crossed with contemporary adventure story. Use with: PLACE 1*, LANGUAGE 2*, INTEREST 5* Qualifiers to indicate if the story is taken from a particular tradition Taip pat žr.: YNRU YFJ

Also class here: Medieval, Dark Age, Arabian, Celtic, Gunpowder, Prehistoric, Wuxia fantasy. Use for: fantasy that incorporates fantastic elements, such as magic or supernatural beings, into recognisable historic settings, periods, cultures etc. Use with: PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers to indicate setting as appropriate
Vadinamoji „tamsioji fantastika“, romantiškos istorijos apie vampyrys ir panašiai. Kai reikia, pateikite ir 5X žymą
Use for: fantasy stories with darker and frightening themes, often incorporating elements of horror or that have a gloomy and threatening atmosphere or a sense of horror and dread

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Contemporary and urban fantasy
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: fantasy set in the present day or recognisably contemporary settings (according to the time period of its creator)

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: liaudies kūryba grįsti pasakojimai
Code.CodeNotes: Pasakos, padavimai, mitai ir legendos, pateikti grožinės literatūros forma Taip pat žr.: YFHG

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Folk and Fairy tales
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Fairy tale retellings, fractured fairy tales. Use for: folk and fairy tales from any culture told in a story form, or retellings of these stories, stories inspired by fairy tales

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Trickster tales
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories that feature a trickster character such as a spirit, a deity, a human or an animal

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Creation, founding, origin stories
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories about the origins or beginnings of peoples, worlds, places, traditions, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Teaching stories
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Cautionary tales, Wisdom tales. Use for: stories that were created for the transmission of wisdom, knowledge, cultural traditions, oral transmission of stories, or stories that warn or caution young people about specific dangers, to teach a lesson or a general moral issue

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: religinė grožinė literatūra
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Faith-inspired or inspirational stories. Use for: fiction that promotes a particular religious, spiritual or visionary message or viewpoint. Use with: 5PG* values from INTEREST 5* Qualifiers or YNR* codes, to indicate the religious tradition, as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Maikų ir paauglių literatūra: meilės istorijos ir melodramos
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories that deal with all kinds of relationships with others; for stories where interpersonal relationships are the main theme; or explore the relationship of the main characters, stories that explore relationships within groups, relationships between young people. Use with: YX* to give details of kinds of relationships as appropriate, for example, YXH for stories about relationships in peer groups or relationships with adults from a young persons perspective, 5PHG for stories about found or chosen family Taip pat žr.: YXHB
Use for: stories where the main or primary topic or theme of the narrative is the friendship between different child or teenage main characters

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Romance and love stories
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: contemporary romance, romantic comedy, romantic drama, stories of first or young love, teenage romances, teenage love-triangles, lost love, unrequited love, high school romance, etc. Use for: stories that are clearly of the romance genre and feature a romantic relationship as the core theme, that are specifically written for teenagers and deal with romance or love stories from a teenage point of view. Use with: YNX* codes as appropriate, with YFT and TIME PERIOD 3* qualifiers for Historical romance, with YFQ for comic romance, etc Taip pat žr.: YFHR

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: šeimyninį gyvenimą vaizduojantys kūriniai
Code.CodeNotes: Jei kūrinyje sąmoningai nagrinėjami tam tikri šeimyninio gyvenimo aspektai, kartu nurodykite ir reikiamą YXF* kodą

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: pasakojimai apie gamtą ir gyvūnus
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories featuring animals, or the natural world, or stories about human interaction or relationships with animals and the natural world, stories about the bond between a child and an animal or pet. Use with: YNN* codes to indicate what type of animal or nature story, for example YNNJ24 for Horse stories or YNN21 for stories about Dogs, YNNH* codes for stories about pets, YNNT for stories about plants or trees

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: humoristinė literatūra
Code.CodeNotes: Naudotinas po atitinkamo žanrą nusakančio (kai tai įmanoma) YF* kodo

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: pasakojimai apie sportą
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: YNW* codes to indicate the sport in the story

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: pasakojimai apie mokyklos gyvenimą
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: back to school, going to a new school, school life, stories principally taking place in and around school, etc. Use with: values from 5L* to indicate what school level as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: istorinis romanas
Code.CodeNotes: Skirta šiuolaikiniams romanams, kurių veiksmas vyksta praeityje, t. y. maždaug iki 1960 m
Naudotinas po kito YF* kodo, nusakančio žanrą (kai įmanoma)

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: eiliuoti pasakojimai
Code.CodeNotes: Naudotinas po kito YF* kodo, nusakančio žanrą (kai įmanoma) Taip pat žr.: YDP YBLB

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: biografinis romanas
Code.CodeNotes: Skirta tikrų žmonių suliteratūrintoms biografijoms ar autobiografijoms

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra: grožine forma perteiktos tikros istorijos
Code.CodeNotes: Tikros istorijos (apie išlikimą, geografinius atradimus, konfliktus ir panašiai), perteiktos grožinės literatūros ar artima šiai forma

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction / Literature / Comics / Graphic novels: Special features and related items
Code.CodeNotes: Use all YFZ* codes with: other YF* code indicating genre or type, YDP for poems, YNDS for plays, or YBCS for picture storybooks or XQ* codes for graphic novels, comic books or manga aimed at children or teenagers. NB: YFZ* codes should not usually be the primary or main subject code. DO NOT USE: YFZ itself - always use YFZ* codes

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Advent calendar stories
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories aimed at children or teenagers, usually in 24 or 25 chapters or stories, meant to be read, heard or seen as a countdown to Christmas through the Advent season. Use with: 5HPDA

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: stories as diaries / journals / letters
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Epistolary fiction. Use for: fiction, often with illustrations, written or drawn in a series of documents, letters, diaries, emails, blogs, social media posts, doodles, etc. Use with: other YF* or XQ* code indicating genre or type
Use for: stories that are reworkings, reimagining’s or retellings of stories, histories or tales. Use with: other YF* or XQ* code indicating genre or type

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: category / serialised stories
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: genre fiction, or comic books usually published on a monthly basis, short, in clearly delineated lines and with a certain number published every month. Use with: other YF* or XQ* code indicating genre or type. YFZR codes should never be the main subject code

Also class here: Illustrated novellas. Use for: short fiction for children or teenagers, usually driven primarily by dialogue and character, and generally accompanied by illustrations in manga/anime or similar styles. Use with: other YF* codes to indicate the genre

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Stories in translation
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: fiction in translation from another language. Use with: YF*, YBCS, YDP, YNDS, or XQ* codes to ensure classification is meaningful beyond the translation of the work itself and with 5T* - Literature of Place Qualifiers as appropriate. DO NOT USE: PLACE 1* or LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers to describe the detail of the original language, this would be described elsewhere and not using Thema. You may still use a PLACE Qualifier if it is relevant to the plot or setting of the book. DO NOT USE: YFZT as the main or primary subject or the only code

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Stories Inspired by or adapted from other media
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories that were published as spin-offs or companions to pre-existing non-book media or merchandise, for example story books based on a popular film franchise, toy, an online game or a TV series. DO NOT USE: for titles that were subsequently made into films etc. Use with: other YF*, YBCS, YDP, YNDS, or XQ* codes indicating genre or type. NB: YFZV codes should never be the main subject code

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Game-related / LitRPG stories
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Literary Role Playing Game, GameLit, RoLit. Use for: fiction that is structured like a videogame, or features the same kind of challenges as would be found in a game, or is about or set in a videogame. Use with: other YF* or XQ* codes as appropriate Taip pat žr.: YFCA

Use for: companion works to popular children’s or teenage fiction series or titles, typically uncritical, such as an atlas or map of a mythical world or fictional universe, a compendium of characters or objects, a guide to the series, art inspired by or taken from the series etc. Use with: other Y* codes or on its own as appropriate, or with X* codes for companion works to graphic novels, comics, manga aimed at children or teenagers

YN* kodai naudotini visiems pažintiniams darbams, kurie nepatenka į kitų kodų aprėptį ir kurie kurti nėra skirti specialiai naudoti per pamokas. Ne grožinės literatūros atveju pateiktinas vien tik reikiamas YN* kodas. Grožinės literatūros atveju, šis kodas pateiktinas po atitinkamo tam tikrą tematiką nusakančio YF* kodo. Kai įmanoma, kartu nurodytinas ir atitinkamas 5A* kodas, žymintis konkrečią amžiaus grupę ar reikiamą turėti žinių lygį. Esant reikalui, pateiktinos ir kitos reikiamos žymos

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: dailė ir dailininkai
Code.CodeNotes: Kai įmanoma, pateikite ir atitinkamą STILIAUS žymą

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: biografijos ir autobiografijos
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: biographies of people from the past and present. Use for: both individual biographies and works that have multiple biographies of different people, titles about heroes or heroines, inspirational figures, famous and everyday people, diaries or journals of individuals. Use with: other YN* codes for particular genres of biography

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: muzika
Code.CodeNotes: Kai įmanoma, pateikite ir atitinkamą STILIAUS žymą

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Musical instruments
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: musical instruction, learning to play the piano, the recorder, the guitar, musical scores, etc. Use with: AVR* codes to indicate specific instruments if more detail is appropriate. NB: if mixing Y* codes with AVR* codes, the Y* code MUST be designated as the Main Subject and sent with a 5A* qualifier
Also class here: song scores, sing along, learning to sing. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: vaidyba, scenos menas
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: circus, acting techniques, stagecraft, theatre, auditions, etc. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate, or with YNB for biographies of performers

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: šokis ir baletas
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: learning to dance. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate, or with YNB for biographies of dancers or dance groups

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: pjesės, dramaturgija
Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: televizija ir kinas
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: titles about making of a film, TV, series, streaming, digital filmmaking, animation, radio, podcasting, etc. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate, or with YNB for biographies of actors, TV, film or video stars, personalities or celebrities

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: bendrasis išsilavinimas ir įvairenybės
Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: bibliotekos, muziejai, mokyklos
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: titles about libraries, museums, schools, using and finding information, guides to using information resources, etc. Use for: informative books about museums, galleries, libraries other cultural centres, and their content

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: istorija ir praeitis
Code.CodeNotes: Biografijoms naudotinas YNB kodas Taip pat žr.: YNB YPJH

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: nuotykių ieškotojai ir nusikaltėliai
Code.CodeNotes: Piratai, lobių medžiotojai ir panašiai Taip pat žr.: YNB

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: atradimai ir mokslinis pažinimas
Code.CodeNotes: Naujų kontinentų, planetų, organizmų, dėsnių ir panašiai atradimai Taip pat žr.: YNB

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: praeities vaikų gyvenimai
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: karyba, mūšiai, ginkluotosios pajėgos
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: soldiers, gladiators, warriors, wars, uniforms, military vehicles. Use with: other YN* codes and PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate Taip pat žr.: YXZW

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Castles and knights
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: medieval warfare

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: darbas ir visuomenė
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: business, the world of work, working or different jobs, specific professions, daily life, everyday occurrences, first jobs, aspects of society or contemporary culture, cultural phenomenon, entrepreneurs, everyday happenings, etc. Use with: YNH for history titles, YXZ* for social issues

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: politika
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles about politicians, politics, political activity, political institutions, government, human rights, political debates, geopolitics explain different political concepts, ideologies, political strategies, political parties or movements, single issues politics, to young people. Use with: YNB and YNH, as appropriate, for biographies of political figures or history titles. NB: YNKA may be used with JP* codes to give extra detail if there is no specific Y* code or qualifier but if mixing YNKA with JP* codes, a Y* code MUST be designated as the Main Subject and sent with a 5A* code

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: teisė, teisėsauga ir nusikaltimai
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works that look at topics around crime, legal matter, law enforcement or are about those that work in these roles, police officers, judges, lawyers, etc or look at criminals or criminality. Use with: YNB for biographies of people in this domain or YNH for history titles

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Medical and emergency services
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: doctors, nurses, health workers, carers, ambulances, paramedics, fire and rescue services, lifeboat services, mountain rescue, a visit to the hospital, the doctor, the dentist, the fire station, etc. Use for: works about the medical, health care and emergency sectors or the people who work in these sectors. Use with: YNB for biographies of people in this domain

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: literatūra, knygos ir rašytojai
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: YNB for biographies of writers

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: vietos ir žmonės
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: travel titles or travel guides for young people. Use with: PLACE 1* or INTEREST 5P* Qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams: šalys, kultūros ir nacionalinis tapatumas
Code.CodeNotes: Tautiniai simboliai, paminklai, drabužiai ir panašiai

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Celebrations, holidays, festivals and special events
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: values from 5H* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate, also use with YNR* codes as appropriate Taip pat žr.: YNR* 5H*

Code.CodeDescription: Pažintinė literatūra vaikams ir paaugliams apie mergaites ir moteris
Code.CodeNotes: Darbai, kuriuose pagrindinis vaidmuo tenka mergaitiškumo ar moteriškumo klausimams

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra asmeniniais ir socialiniais klausimais: draugai ir draugystė

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Life skills and choices
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: manners, behaviour, dilemmas, consequences, responsibilities, skills for interacting with modern life, other people, following or not following rules, getting into trouble, taking responsibility for actions, assuming the consequences, not using violence, not hitting, kicking or biting, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra asmeniniais ir socialiniais klausimais: nėštumas paauglystėje

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra asmeniniais ir socialiniais klausimais: narkotikai ir priklausomybė
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: topics around substance addiction, alcohol abuse, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Anxiety, depression and self-harm

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Multicultural
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works on social and cultural topics linked to multiculturalism, pluriculturalism, biculturalism and multicultural, pluricultural or bicultural societies

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra asmeniniais ir socialiniais klausimais: rasizmas ir multikultūralizmas
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: xenophobia, race relations. Use for: works about discrimination and prejudice based on skin colour, race or ethnic origin, or prejudices based on the perception that someone is foreign or from outside the community, and issues of inequality and discrimination, as well as measures to address racism. Use with: YNH for historical topics Taip pat žr.: JBFA1

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Diversity, equality, equity and inclusion
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: books that deal with these topics and stories with a particularly diverse cast of characters, or which illustrate accessibility, social justice, equity, diversity, or inclusivity (DEI) within the context of the story without necessarily being the subject of the story. Use with: YF* codes for stories and values from 5P* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Prejudice and intolerance
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: discrimination, injustice, the judgements of others. Use with: YNH for historical topics

Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: use of violent or abusive language. Use for: works that explore these topics, often titles aimed at explaining or helping young people understand or deal with these topics. Use with: YF* when it is the major element of the story

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Abuse / exploitation
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: physical, mental, emotional or sexual abuse, coercive control, domestic abuse, or works aimed at young people about criminal exploitation, debt bondage, exploitation of vulnerable children by criminal gangs

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Bullying and harassment
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: online trolling and bullying, coercion, cyberbullying, cyberstalking, physical or verbal bullying or harassment, relational bullying, collective bullying or mobbing, bullies and accomplices, victims of bullying, effects of bullying and harassment, bystander effect, school bullying, victimisation

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Violence
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Knife violence, gun violence, bombs, violent acts, acts of terrorism, kidnapping, violent threats, violent rampages. Use for: works aimed at young people dealing with physical violence or conflict involving weapons, helping young people deal with knife crime, with gun violence, stabbings, shootings, violent gang crimes, school shootings, violence of war, for works helping young people avoid violence, or deal with the trauma of weapons related violence

Code.CodeNotes: Kaip elgtis su nepažįstamaisiais, saugumas keliuose, saugumas namuose ir panašiai

Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: fugitives, escapees. Use for: works that look at young people that run away and reasons around this, running away from home, or family or school or escaping things like repression, slavery, conflict, etc. Use with: YF* codes for stories about runaways, with YNB for biographies of runaways, or YNH for historical approaches Taip pat žr.: YXZM

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra asmeniniais ir socialiniais klausimais: pamokų praleidinėjimas ir mokyklinės problemos

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Growing up / coming of age
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles that deal with the changes from childhood or youth to adulthood, such as taking on adult responsibilities, career choices, character growth, gaining independence, self-reliance, moving away from home, going to university, first experience of love, etc. Use with: YF* for coming of age fiction, YXA* codes for works about changes to the body, or sex, YXHL for first love, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Vaikų ir paauglių literatūra socialiniais klausimais
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: social activism, general works on social justice. Use for: titles that deal directly with the topics or explain debates around social issues for young people. Use with: other YX* codes to give greater detail; YF* fiction codes for stories that are about these topics. NB: YXZ may be used with JBF* codes if there are no more precise Y* codes but if mixing YXZ with JBF* codes, a Y* code MUST be designated as the Main Subject and sent with a 5A* qualifier

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage social topics: Activism / activists

Use with: other YN* or YX* codes to give greater detail and with YNB for biographies of activists

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage social topics: Identity / belonging

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage social topics: Peace / reconciliation

Visada, kai įmanoma, pasirinkite atitinkamą 5* kodą (ar kodus), tiesiog „5“ nenaudokite

Use all 5A* age codes for: defining the Y* or X* codes – 5A* age numbers are used instead of named codes, such as juvenile, middle grade, young adult, as these have different meanings in different countries or languages. Select one 5A* code indicating a general guideline starting or base interest age of the content in any works aimed primarily at children or teenagers. All Y* codes (except YP* which use 4* codes) MUST be accompanied by one 5A* qualifier code to give guidance of interest age, for example: book content for an audience of 9 to 12 age group, should use 5AK, as the lower age; content of interest to teenagers should use 5AP or 5AQ; content for older teenagers and young adults should use 5AS, 5AT or 5AU as appropriate. 5AR, 5AX and 5AZ can be used with any relevant subject code. All 5A* codes can be used with X* subject codes if the Comic book is aimed at children or teenagers. DO NOT USE: 5A itself – always use 5A* codes. NB: Greater detail of age range, reading age, interest age etc would be communicated in other metadata

Also class here: High-low readers, Hi-Lo content aimed at children or teenagers. Use for: books that are specially written for or considered suitable for young people who do not want to read, have difficulty reading, or are struggling to read. Usually these books will have a higher interest age and a lower reading age. Content is usually aimed at a particular interest age but the language used is purposefully slightly simpler than most average content aimed at the same interest age in that language, so that it is easier to read or listen to than other titles. These are often titles in specific named collections and will often have notions of levels of difficulty associated with them by the publisher and / or may be accompanied by indications of complexity. Use with: one other 5A* Interest age qualifier. Prefer: 5AX for reluctant adult readers or 5AZ for accessible content and 4L codes for second language titles Taip pat žr.: 5AX 5AZ 4L*

Code.CodeDescription: Interest age: from c 17 years to c 29 years
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works aimed specifically at older teens and young adults in their 20s, those who are newly adult, emerging adulthood. This age group may be referred to in some places as young adults or sometimes as new adults. The content is specifically created for and about this group but can also appeal to other groups as well. Prefer: 5LKE for titles about this age group. DO NOT USE: with Y* codes Taip pat žr.: 5LKE

Also class here: High-low readers, Hi-Lo content aimed at adults. Use for: books that are specifically aimed at adult literacy or helping adult readers with reading difficulties or books that are suitable for adult readers who are not confident in their reading abilities or suitable for the newly literate. Content is aimed at adult interests but the language used is purposefully slightly simpler than most average content aimed at adults so that it is easier to read or listen to than other titles

Code.CodeDescription: Content adapted or suitable for people with learning / communication difficulties or impairments
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: indicating works where the content is specifically adapted for, or purposefully written for, or aimed at people, regardless of age, with special or additional needs, who may have difficulty in accessing or reading the content of most titles. This could include content specifically adapted for people with, for example, dyslexia and other reading or learning disabilities, cognitive impairments or disorders, memory disorders, dementia or Alzheimer’s, visual or other sensory impairments, profound and multiple learning disabilities, etc. Use with: 5PM* Qualifiers as appropriate

Use all 5H* codes for: indicating that the content of a work is largely about or relates to the holiday, event or season, for example a book featuring a Christmas story would use 5HPD or a book about birthdays for children would use 5HKA, a romance story that is all about summer could use 5HRB. DO NOT USE: to create list of suggested titles for sale at a particular season (this is information that is conveyed elsewhere in the supply chain) if those titles do not have content relating to the 5H* code

Use for: content that is about public or civic holidays or celebrations in general or about a holiday or celebration that does not have a more precise code. Use with: 1* PLACE qualifiers when associated with a particular area

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to the stages of life
Code.CodeNotes: Use all 5L* codes for: indicating the content of the work has major themes, topics or storylines relating to or specifically about, or from the perspective of, the main stages of life, or the process of ageing, growing up, the cycle of life from birth to death, or fiction done from the point of view of a person or persons of that stage of life. A novel about teenage anxiety could use 5LF, a romance set amongst students at university could use 5LKE, or a book about Yoga for seniors could use 5LKS. DO NOT USE: to indicate a targeted audience for marketing purposes, the content should be primarily about this stage of life or age group or told from the point of view of that age group
Also class here: babies, infants and toddlers. Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about infancy
Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about childhood or being a child, or stories told from the point of view of a child

Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or primarily about the years between childhood and adolescence, the passage from being a child to being a teenager, or stories told from the point of view of the preteen or preadolescence

Also class here: growing from a teenager to being an adult. Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about adolescence or being a teenager, the teenage years, the issues, changes, developments that are common for teenagers. Use with: YF* or F* codes when the main themes of a novel are specifically related to the teenage years, being a teenager, specifically from a teenagers point of view, or issues connected with adolescence and use with non-fiction codes for studies, themes or content about teenagers

Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about being an older teenager (roughly 15 to 19 years old), the later teenage years, the issues, changes, developments that are common for older teenagers, also referred to as young adults in some circumstances, post-adolescents. Use with: YF* or F* codes when the main themes of a novel are specifically related to the later teenage years, being an older teenager, specifically from an older teenager’s point of view, or issues connected with late or post adolescence and use with non-fiction codes for studies, themes or content about older teenagers
Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about adulthood or being an adult, life as an adult, etc

Also class here: post-teens, new adult, young adulthood, twenty something, emerging adulthood, etc. Use for: material that is primarily about, or from the perspective of, or has major or principal themes relating to the stage of life spanning from the late teens through to the mid- or late twenties, often centred on topics around becoming an adult or coming of age, progressing from being a teenager to being an adult, those who are newly adult, learning to become an adult. Use with: FR* for ‘New Adult Romance’ or FRG for ‘College Romance’, FP for ‘New Adult Erotica’, FM* for ‘New Adult Fantasy’, etc. when the main themes of a novel are specifically related to this stage of life and use with non-fiction codes for studies, themes or content about this passage from teenager to adult
Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about midlife or middle age

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to late adulthood / old age
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: seniors, elders, third agers, retirees, pensioners, older persons. Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about old age or later life. Use with: F* or YF* codes when the main themes of a novel are specifically related to this phase of life, for example, FR* for romance in later life, or YFN for a story about an elderly relative, and use with non-fiction codes for studies, themes or content about this stage of life

Code.CodeDescription: Susiję su specifinėmis grupėmis ir kultūromis
Code.CodeNotes: Use all 5P* codes for: indicating the content of the work has major themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspective of, or are specifically about the particular group of people. DO NOT USE: to indicate a target audience for marketing purposes, nor to identify the origin of the author, unless this relates to the content of the work
Kodus 5PB* naudokite medžiagai, kuri yra susijusi su specifine tautine grupe, gali ją dominti arba yra apie ją. Taip pat pateikite ir atitinkamą JBSL* kodą ir kitus reikiamus kodus

Use for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspective of, or about, any groups of people or persons from any of the multiple, diverse and different groups or cultures of the various Indigenous communities, Peoples and Nations and where there is no more precise code. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate to indicate location or with LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers when the language identifies the group, for example, a work about the Indigenous peoples of the Americas, use with 1K, for the Indigenous peoples of Mexico, use with 1KLCM, the Indigenous peoples of Peru, use with 1KLSR, for the Indigenous Peoples of the Arctic use with 1MTN, for Indigenous peoples of Siberia, use with 1FCS, for Indigenous peoples associated with the South -Western US States, use with 1KBB-US-WM, etc Taip pat žr.: 5PB-US-E 5PB-NZ-A 5PB-AU-A 5PBS

Also class here: Melanesians, Micronesians, Polynesians peoples, including, but not limited to, Kanaks, Papuans, Indigenous Hawaiians, Kānaka Maoli, Fijians, iTaukei, Ni-Vanuatu, Chamorro, Chuukese, Rapa Nui, Samoans, Tahitians. Use for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspectives of, or about, any of the diverse groups of people or persons, who are part of an Indigenous Pacific Island group or heritage

Use for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspectives of, or about, members of any Indigenous community who gained respect and stature through their lives allowing them to have a leadership role

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to peoples or groups of multiple heritage / culture
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: material where the major or principal themes, topics or storylines relate to, or from the perspectives of, or are about any of the diverse groups of people or persons of multiple heritage or cultures

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to migrant groups / diaspora communities or peoples / groups with shared heritage
Code.CodeNotes: Use all 5PBC* codes for: material where the major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspectives of, or about, (historical and recent) diverse groups of people or persons who have migrated or were exiled or displaced from one part of the world to another; or are part of a diaspora community and who maintain a strong and distinct identity and cultural shared heritage associated with another geographical or cultural area within their present place of residence. Use all 5PBC* codes with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate, to indicate the geographical area that is the subject of the work, usually where that group is now, for example, a title about Syrian migrant communities in Sweden, use with 1DNS, or a title about Guatemalan migrant workers in Mexico, use with 1KLCM or a study of German exiled writers of the mid-twentieth century, in the USA, use with 1KBB Taip pat žr.: 5PBD

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to people of the Middle Eastern diasporas / heritage
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: diaspora peoples of Western Asia, Anatolia, the Arabian Peninsula. Use for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspectives of, or about, (historical and recent) Middle Eastern diasporas, or any of the diverse groups or individuals of Middle Eastern heritage living in another geographical area or culture. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate, to indicate the scope of the geographical area covered by the group or individual or topic in the work, for example, a biography of an Armenian family in France, use with 1DDF*, or a novel about Turkish migrants in Germany, use with 1DFG*, or a history of Arab Americans in Detroit, use with 1KBB-US-MLGD. Prefer: 1FB* PLACE qualifiers, without 5PBCB, for works about peoples, groups or individuals who live in a particular Middle Eastern country or region, or works about peoples of the Middle East Taip pat žr.: 1FB*

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to people of the North African / Maghreb diasporas / heritage
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspectives of, or about, (historical and recent) North African diasporas or any of the diverse groups or individuals of North African or Maghrebian heritage living in another geographical area or culture. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate, to indicate the scope of the geographical area covered by the group or individual or topic in the work, for example, a novel dealing with the experience of being Kabyle in the suburbs of Lyon, use with 1DDF-FR-VFA. Prefer: 1HB* PLACE qualifiers without 5PBCD for works about peoples, groups or individuals who live in a particular North African country or region, or works about peoples of North Africa Taip pat žr.: 5PBD 1HB*

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to people of the South Asian diasporas / heritage
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspectives of, or about, (historical and recent) South Asian diasporas, or any of the diverse groups or individuals of South Asian heritage living in another geographical area or culture. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate, to indicate the scope of the geographical area covered by the group or individual or topic in the work, for example, a teen novel about a Tamil Australian, use with 1MBF or a book about desi music in the USA use with 1KBB. Prefer: 1FK* PLACE qualifiers without 5PBCG for works about peoples, groups or individuals who live in a particular South Asian country or region, or works about peoples of South Asia Taip pat žr.: 1FK*

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to people of the South East Asian diasporas / heritage

NB: If using 5X with a Y* code it is highly recommended that an explanation of the reason for using it be sent in a descriptive text elsewhere in the titles metadata and that a suitable 5A * Age qualifier be used

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to special / particular aspects of the content
Code.CodeNotes: Use all 5Y* codes for: describing a specific and very particular aspect of the content (not the format) of a title, that is not covered by other qualifiers. DO NOT USE: 5Y itself - always use 5Y* codes

Use for: works that are purposefully written to actively challenge a gender stereotype or norm around gender roles or includes positive representation of non-stereotypical gender roles, e.g. YBC* or YF* codes for children’s stories. NB: Further details of why this qualifier is being used should be sent in other descriptive metadata

Code.CodeDescription: Content relating to body acceptance / body positivity
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works that encourage body acceptance or body neutrality, that show a diverse range of body types, sizes, shapes, that show positive roles for characters, people, or groups of different body types

Code.CodeDescription: Content relates specifically to anthropomorphic characters
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: content that has anthropomorphic characters or uses anthropomorphism as a literary device to tell a story, content that has stories that use the attribution of human traits, emotions, or intentions to non-human entities, such as animals or plants

Code.CodeDescription: Content relates specifically to multiple perspectives
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: multiperspectivity, polyperspectivity. Use for: content that is shown from more than one perspective, for fiction that uses multiple narrators or a multiple narrative, or for non-fiction where the subject or events are evaluated from multiple different perspectives or points of view
